#### 1. Camurati-Engelmann disease type 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.776)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11768)

**Proposed mechanism:** TGFB2 (HGNC:11768) —INCREASES→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1237001); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1237001) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue development (HP:0003198); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1237001) —LEADS_TO→ Bone development abnormality (HP:0000924). Gain-of-function variants in TGFB2 lead to overactivation of the TGF-beta signaling pathway, which in turn affects connective tissue and bone development, manifesting as overlapping phenotypes in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of loss-of-function variants in TGFB2 as the sole cause of either MONDO:0013897 or MONDO:0011690 would refute the proposed gain-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the TGF-beta signaling pathway could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions, provided the specific downstream effects can be modulated to alleviate disease phenotypes without causing adverse effects.

#### 2. Glanzmann thrombasthenia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.451)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in ITGA2B (null) —DISRUPTS→ ITGA2B (HGNC:6008); ITGA2B (HGNC:6008) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-8939027); Pathogenic variant in ITGA2B (null) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal bleeding (HP:00114110); Pathogenic variant in ITGB3 (null) —DISRUPTS→ ITGB3 (HGNC:6007); ITGB3 (HGNC:6007) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb beta-3 signaling (REACT:R-HSA-8939027); Pathogenic variant in ITGB3 (null) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873). Pathogenic variants in ITGA2B and ITGB3 lead to the disruption of the Integrin alpha-IIb beta-3 signaling pathway. This disruption causes a loss-of-function in platelet aggregation and adhesion, manifesting as abnormal bleeding (HP:00114110) in MONDO:0013897, and impaired clot formation leading to thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873) in Glanzmann thrombasthenia.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in either ITGA2B or ITGB3 with a significantly high allele frequency (e.g., > 1%) in gnomAD for the relevant population would falsify the hypothesis that these variants are causal for rare disease phenotypes. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving the integrin signaling pathway could lead to the development of targeted therapies for bleeding disorders, potentially by modulating integrin function or downstream signaling components.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of amyloid pathology or lack of APP mutations in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0013897 would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a pathogenic variant in APP with a population frequency > 0.1% for the specific disease-causing variants.)_

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGA2B (HGNC:6047) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 complex formation and function (GO:0007161); ITGB3 (HGNC:6055) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 complex formation and function (GO:0007161); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 complex formation and function (GO:0007161) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hemostasis (HP:00114102); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 complex formation and function (GO:0007161) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); Integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 complex formation and function (GO:0007161) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001892).
